title: SO2 next-hour prediction - Beijing, Aotizhongxin station (UCI)
summary: We predicted SO2 one hour ahead using the Beijing, Aotizhongxin station (UCI) data. XGBoost did best on the validation period, so we used it. On the test period (12 May 2016 to 28 Feb 2017) its average error was 1.780 µg/m³. Just repeating the last hour's value gave 1.702 µg/m³, so the model was 4.6% worse. 106 episodes were flagged: 62 look like unusual pollution, 5 look like data problems and 39 are unclear.
how_it_was_made: Read the hourly data and treated empty cells and -200 as missing.

Built the inputs: hour, weekday, the reading 1 hour before, the reading 2 hours before, the reading 3 hours before, the reading at the same time the day before, temperature, air pressure, dew point, rain, wind speed.
Split the timeline in order: first 60% to train, next 20% to choose the model, last 20% to test.
Tried Linear Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost. Each predicts how much the level changes in the next hour.
Flagged test hours where the miss was more than 8.95 µg/m³ (bigger than 95% of the misses on the validation period).
By design this limit flags 5% of the validation hours; on the test period it flagged 3.1% of hours. So the number of episodes partly depends on where the limit is set.

Grouped flagged hours that were less than 3 hours apart and checked each group: missing inputs or a gap, a stuck reading, or a sudden jump that nothing else shared mean a data problem; other pollutants moving the same way at the same time mean unusual pollution; anything else is unclear.
patterns: Most episodes peaked around 00:00, 02:00 and 23:00, and 72% fell on weekdays, about what you'd expect, so they are spread across the week. The busiest month was Jan 2017 with 37 episodes.
